tasks.task: Copy edit a draft with the changes marked

items.when: When a client sends a draft and a deadline, to agree the level of edit and run it in order
Before editing anything longer than a few pages, to fix spellings, capitals and number style
When the draft needs to be clear, consistent and correct while keeping the writer's voice
When the client has a style guide and wants grammar and punctuation fixed against it
When sentences are correct but cluttered, to find the point and cut what does no work
Before handing back, to catch a term, name or number written two ways

tasks.task: Proofread final copy before it is published

items.when: When the text is final and only errors should change, not style
When you want it corrected in the writer's own voice with a log of every change
When the writer wants a list of slips and term clashes with nothing rewritten
When the copy is laid out, to check type size, spacing and line length on the page
When the client works in a browser or Word and wants a second pass in their own tool

tasks.task: Rewrite a text in plain language for a named reader

items.when: When a text must reach about a grade 8 reader and keep every legal, safety and money point
When a draft needs plain words with each cut explained
When the piece has two audiences, to try a version experts respect and newcomers follow
When the text is a contract and the reader needs what each side owes in two minutes
When long words and passive sentences hide who does what
When the rewrite is done, to check how hard it still is for the reader named

tasks.task: Give a structural edit of a long draft

items.when: Before the critique, to name the one main idea and what fights it
When a report, guide, chapter or proposal needs its order, gaps and repeats assessed
When the draft needs a new outline, to propose an order that holds a reader
When the argument wanders, to put the answer first and group the reasons under it
When the writer needs straight feedback that names the weak lines
When the restructured draft is back, to edit and re-check it until it passes

tasks.task: Cut a draft to a word limit without losing the point

items.when: When a piece is over its limit and every word feels necessary to the writer
When you are unsure how deep to cut, to see a light trim first with a log of every cut
When the piece is far over, to cut whole parts that do not serve the main idea
When a passage is wordy and should say the same in shorter, harder sentences
When the cut piece is an abstract, to check it still matches the results

tasks.task: Build a style sheet and run a consistency check

items.when: When a team keeps writing the same words different ways
Before the final proofread of a long document, above all one with several writers
When the client has a voice and style guide, to rank where the draft departs from it
When the document is technical, to list term clashes and jargon as well as slips

tasks.task: Flag claims that need a source and check the facts

items.when: Before publishing, to list every claim about numbers, research, health, money or law
When the flagged claims must be checked against trusted sources
When a claim rests on one study, to see its biases, weak statistics and evidence grade
When the reference list is messy, to get clean, checked references

tasks.task: Write a fair peer review of a paper or study

items.when: When an author wants the review a fair journal reviewer would give, before submitting
When you have the manuscript and want a claim check, a methods review and a kind report
When one result carries the paper, to test how strong the evidence is
When the conclusions run ahead of the data, to ask what the data really shows
When the abstract may promise more than the results give

tasks.task: Plan the revision of a paper before submission

items.when: When a paper is ready to submit or has come back, to run review and revision in order
When the review is done and must turn into a ranked list of revisions
When the paper is still being drafted and must fit one journal from the start
When the review finds thin support, to gather current sources and competing findings

tasks.task: Plan a response to journal reviewer comments

items.when: When a paper has a revise-and-resubmit decision and every comment needs an answer
When each comment must be tied to the manuscript and the evidence that answers it
During revision, to track which comments are answered and which are still open
When the response and the revised paper must go back together

tasks.task: Check a paper against the journal's rules

items.when: When the journal is named, to get its template, page limits and anonymity rules
Before submitting, to check each citation against the reference list and the papers
When references are in the wrong form or incomplete
When figures do not meet the journal's rules for clarity, colour or uncertainty

tasks.task: Edit a draft so it sounds like its writer, not a machine

items.when: When the client has a set voice, to fix off-voice words without touching the claims
When lines sound machine made, to fix each one and see a score
When you need the list of stock phrases and structures to look for

tasks.task: Edit a story or novel manuscript

items.when: When a story or book draft has rested and is ready to be revised step by step
When you want the story checked against plain-fiction rules with each fault named
When the manuscript is long, to list name slips, age errors and things out of their time
When the talk sounds stiff, to test each line and fix the worst
When scenes feel flat, to mark what changes in each one and which do nothing
When the author wants structure, character arcs and pacing checked against named models
When the draft over-explains and should trust the situation and the reader

tasks.task: Edit an article, web page or long email

items.when: When an owner writes well but rambles and the piece needs tightening
When it is web or marketing copy, to tighten it in passes for clarity, proof and the ask
When it is a long email, to get cuts, a pacing map and subject fixes
When the title is weak, to offer the writer several angles
When there are several titles, to score each read alone

tasks.task: Edit technical documentation for a named reader

items.when: When an English technical document needs slips, term clashes and jargon listed
When findings are written for experts and the reader is not one
When product names, units and commands must be written one way throughout

tasks.task: Write honest feedback an author can act on

items.when: When the writer asked for the truth and needs the weak parts named plainly
When the feedback must cover order, gaps and what to cut, not line fixes
When the writer is a student and comments must turn into clear next steps

tasks.task: Edit a proposal or grant section to the funder's rules

items.when: When a section is over the funder's word limit
When it is an application, to check each claim against the rules and the evidence
When it is a research grant, to know the funder's rules before editing

tasks.task: Write an abstract or summary of a long piece

items.when: Before writing, to pull out the piece's claims, evidence and gaps
When a long analysis needs one page with the answer first
When the length is not fixed, to compare summaries at different levels of detail
When the abstract is drafted, to list anything it overclaims

tasks.task: Review a thesis or dissertation chapter

items.when: When a thesis needs a fair review of what is strong and what is weak
When a chapter should be read the way an examiner would read it
When the defence is near and every claim needs a page reference

always.when: Last pass on anything you hand back, with a log of every change
After your own rewrites, so the edit does not add machine-sounding lines
When an edit changes a fact, name or number, to check the new wording is still true

helpers.when: When technical documents need writing or restructuring, not only editing
When the text must be translated, or a translation checked against its source
When flagged claims need sources found and read, not only marked
When a bid or grant needs its argument rebuilt, not only cut
When the draft is too thin to edit and needs to be written in the client's voice
When the edited report needs a page layout or a deck version

gaps: No library item copy edits general prose with marked changes and author queries; the editors are for sales copy or light proofreading
No library item builds a style sheet or checks hyphens, capitals and numbers across a long document; the kit carries this alone
No library item gives a developmental edit of a non-fiction book or report beyond an outline
No library item edits English written by a non-native speaker, or checks a translation against its source for ordinary text
No library item checks for inclusive or sensitive language
No library item checks a paper against reporting checklists for trials, reviews or surveys
No library item checks for copied text or overlap with published work
No library item converts references between styles such as APA, Chicago and Harvard
No library item returns edits as Word tracked changes
